title: Mukesh Ambani Reclaims Asia's Richest Title as Forbes Puts Wealth at $88.8 Billion
excerpt: An updated Forbes real-time listing credits Ambani with an $8.5 billion Monday gain, moving him past ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming ($84 billion) to the top of Asia's rich list at 23rd globally.
body:
• Mukesh Ambani has reclaimed the title of Asia's richest person on Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, overtaking ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming.
  • Forbes' updated listing puts Ambani's net worth at $88.8 billion and his global rank at 23rd; Zhang stands 25th with an estimated $84 billion, and Gautam Adani 26th with $79.12 billion.
  • The updated listing credits Ambani with an $8.5 billion gain on Monday — up from the $6.3 billion in Forbes' earlier snapshot — after Reliance Industries shares surged nearly 12%.
  • For Reliance shareholders, the stock's 11.6% Monday jump was its strongest session in more than six years, following quarterly profit that beat analyst expectations.

Mukesh Ambani, chairman and managing director of Reliance Industries, has reclaimed the title of Asia's richest person, overtaking ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming, according to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list as reported on Tuesday. The change at the top of the regional ranking is the new development in the Reliance story: a later update to the Forbes list raised the estimated size of Ambani's Monday gain and moved him ahead of Zhang, the former chief executive of TikTok's parent company.

Forbes puts Ambani's estimated net worth at $88.8 billion, with a 10.5% jump in his fortune lifting him to 23rd place on the global billionaire index. Zhang ranks 25th with an estimated net worth of $84 billion, according to the updated listing reported by TradingView News. Gautam Adani, the next Indian on the list, was ranked 26th with a fortune of $79.12 billion in Forbes' earlier update.

Why the Gain Figure Changed

Readers who saw Monday's first reports will notice a different number. Forbes' earlier snapshot on November 2 recorded a gain of $6.3 billion, or 7.85%, already making Ambani the world's biggest billionaire wealth gainer that day — well ahead of Spanish retail billionaire Amancio Ortega's $1.7 billion gain and China's Zhong Shanshan's $1.5 billion, according to YourStory's report of that update. The later listing put the Monday gain at $8.5 billion. Both snapshots land on the same total: a net worth of $88.8 billion. Real-time billionaire rankings recalculate as share prices move, so the daily gain attached to a closing fortune can change between updates even when the closing fortune does not.

What Drove the Reliance Rally

The ranking change rests on one trading session. Reliance Industries shares jumped 11.6% on Monday, their strongest session in more than six years, closing at the day's high as the biggest gainer on the benchmark Nifty 50 index. The rally added more than $19 billion to Reliance's market capitalisation in the session. Reliance remains India's most valuable firm, with a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 17 trillion (about $186 billion).

The shares moved after Reliance's September-quarter results, which showed consolidated net profit rising 40.6% year on year to Rs 25,548 crore, ahead of analyst expectations. Refining core earnings surged 68% in the quarter and Jio Platforms' core earnings rose 16.6%, while profitability in the retail business remained under pressure. Following the results, an analyst at Avendus Spark upgraded the stock from "reduce" to "add," and Reliance now has no "hold" or "sell" recommendations from analysts for the first time since 2017, according to Bloomberg data cited in the reports.

The Wider Picture

Reliance operates across petrochemicals, oil and gas, telecom, retail, media and financial services. Its telecom and broadband arm, Jio Platforms, listed in October 2026 and reached a market capitalisation of $137 billion, making it India's second-most valuable company after its parent, according to Forbes' profile cited by YourStory. Ambani has also announced plans to invest $110 billion in AI infrastructure across India over the next seven years.

Forbes' real-time figures are estimates that move with the share price, and the Asia ranking has changed hands before: Zhang first moved ahead of Ambani earlier this year. Whether Ambani holds the top spot will depend on how Reliance shares trade from here — the same force that put him back on top in a single session can move the ranking again just as quickly.
